sentences.text: The present petition has been filed seeking quashing of FIR No.441/2016 under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 registered at Police Station Jamia Nagar on the ground of settlement.
2. The petitioner is the husband of the respondent no.2.
The marriage of the petitioner and the respondent no.2 was solemnized on 8th October, 2013 as per Muslim rites and ceremonies.
No child was born out of the wedlock.
3. Dispute arose between the petitioner and the respondent no.2, which resulted in filing of the present FIR by the respondent no.2 against the petitioner.

4. The parties have settled all their disputes in terms of the Memorandum of Understanding (MOU)
dated 16th August, 2017, which has been filed as Annexure P-3 to the petition.

sentences.text: In terms of the aforesaid MOU, a sum of Rs.5,00,000/- has been duly paid to the respondent no.2.
The MOU records the details of the payment made to the respondent no.2 by way of demand drafts.
6. Counsel for the petitioner submits that both the petitioner and the respondent no.2 have since remarried and the respondent no. 2 resides at Moradabad.
7. Initially, the respondent no.2 appeared in the present petition.
However, subsequently the respondent no.2 has not been appearing.
Earlier, attempts were made for the respondent no.2 to appear through video conferencing, which were not successful.

8. Considering the above settlement between the parties and the chances of conviction of the petitioner being remote and bleak, there is no use continuing with proceedings of the present FIR as it would be a misuse of the process of the Court and an unnecessary burden on the State exchequer.
Hence, it would be in the interest of justice to quash the aforementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
9. Consequently, the FIR No. 441/2016 registered at Police Station Jamia Nagar and the proceedings pursuant thereto are quashed.
10. The petition stands disposed of.

AMIT BANSAL, J.
OCTOBER 17, 2023 rt
